cards.title: Many fast tests, few slow ones
cards.body: The test pyramid: a wide base of unit tests that run in milliseconds, fewer integration tests, and a thin top of end-to-end tests. The shape keeps the suite fast enough to run on every change.

cards.title: A stub answers, a mock checks
cards.body: A stub returns canned data so the code under test can run. A mock also records the calls and fails the test when the expected calls did not happen. A fake is a working light version, such as an in-memory database.

cards.title: A unit test with no dependency
cards.body: Node has a test runner since version 18. node --test finds the test files and runs them; --watch runs them again on each save.

cards.title: A test that reads the clock will fail one day
cards.body: Code that calls Date.now() or new Date() inside the logic gives a test that passes today and fails at midnight, at a month end or in another time zone. Pass the time in as a parameter, as you would any other input.

cards.title: In test-driven development, what comes right after a failing test?
options: Write the least code that makes it pass
cards.body: Red, green, refactor: a failing test, the least code to make it pass, then clean-up with the test as a safety net.

cards.title: A suite has 100% line coverage. What does that prove?
options: Every line ran during the tests
Every branch was taken both ways
cards.body: Line coverage proves that a line ran, not that a test checked its result. Branch coverage and mutation testing measure more of what the assertions really catch.

cards.title: The Practical Test Pyramid
cards.body: Ham Vocke's article on martinfowler.com: which tests to write at each layer of a real service, with examples of unit, integration, contract and UI tests.
